title: Field signal lode and ask maps — consolidated synthesis
content:
Purpose
----
This is a compact synthesis of recent field signals (Aug–Nov 2027) with clustered asks, rough impact estimates, proposed product owners, and pragmatic tradeoffs. Goal: give PMs and ENG a quick, actionable map — not a polished roadmap.

Methodology notes
----
- Sources: post-demo feedback, support tickets, recorded onboarding sessions, 3 enterprise interviews, two pilot retros.
- Triage lens: frequency x pain x strategic alignment (Redwood positioning: production-first inference).
- We captured raw customer language where helpful; quotes preserved to show intent.

Topline themes (ranked by combined signal)
----
1) Predictable tail latency and SLAs for bursty workloads (high freq, high pain)
   - Customer ask: "We need tail latency guarantees when traffic spikes — our SLAs can’t tolerate 2–3s hiccups."
   - Where it hits: Hosted API + Dedicated
   - Why now: several customers hitting scale as they roll to prod; SRE risk.
   - Quick win: expose per-tenant percentile telemetry in Console (90/95/99) + automated alert template. (owner: observability)
   - Longer play: soft isolation lanes + reservation-burst config to reduce noisy-neighbor risk. (owner: dedicated)

2) Model fallback and graceful degradation policy tooling (medium freq, high strategic)
   - Ask: "Automatically fall back to a cheaper/quantized variant when capacity constrained — but preserve hallucination/safety budgets."
   - Where: Routing, Optimize, Serving runtime
   - Tradeoffs: fallback can change output characteristics; customers want explainability of degradations.
   - Suggested MVP: route-level policy with labeled fallback variants + confidence tagging in responses. (owner: serving-runtime + routing team)

3) Prompt-level cost visibility and attribution (medium freq, medium pain)
   - Ask: token-level cost breakdown per call, with sample prompts mapped to cost buckets.
   - Why valuable: helps customers tune behavior and justify infra spend internally.
   - Quick win: add an exportable per-route cost CSV and sample slow/high-cost calls UI. (owner: console)

4) Embedded model parity for on-prem/private (lower freq, high enterprise impact)
   - Ask: same model variants available in Private as Hosted (quantized equivalents, matching perf profiles).
   - Barrier: licensing + packaging + kernel compatibility across HW.
   - Recommended: shipping a curated "private compat" model pack and a compatibility checklist. (owner: private-deployments + applied-ml)

5) Improved dev ergonomics around streaming + function-calls (choppy notes, frequent asks from PLG)
   - Common friction: inconsistent event ordering between SDKs; tests flake in CI.
   - MVP: add deterministic event ordering doc + SDK test harness snippets. (owner: dev-ex)
Representative customer quotes (verbatim, anonymized)
----
- "Our application has short bursts at end-of-day. We can handle steady-state latency but those microspikes blow past our SLA."
- "We need a visible and supported fallback — telling product teams we degraded without a way to track it is toxic."
- "Sometimes we just want a cheap quantized inference that matches our hosted results closely for offline batch runs."

Clustered asks + rough prioritization (1–3 weeks quick-win vs 1–3 months project)
----
A. Telemetry & alerting for tail latency — Priority: P0 quick-win (1–3w)
   - Deliverable: per-route percentile dashboard + email/Slack alert template + sample playbook.
   - Impact: immediate reduction in escalations; gives SREs confidence.

B. Route-level fallback policies (policy UI + runtime enforcement) — Priority: P1 (2–3m)
   - Deliverable: policy schema, Console UI stub, runtime switch, audit log of fallbacks.
   - Open Qs: how to present quality deltas; what tags do customers want on fallback events?

C. Cost attribution exports and sample tuning guide — Priority: P1 quick-win (2–4w)
   - Deliverable: CSV export, UI sample list of top-10 expensive calls, internal customer-facing tuning FAQ.

D. Private deployable model pack and compatibility guide — Priority: P2 (3–6m)
   - Deliverable: curated archive, quantization notes, verification scripts.

E. Streaming + function-calls stability kit — Priority: P2 quick-win (3–5w)
   - Deliverable: SDK snippets, deterministic ordering doc, e2e test harness repo link.

Risk notes and constraints
----
- Fallback transparency vs product simplicity: exposing too many knobs will confuse PLG customers; propose a "basic" vs "advanced" mode.
- Private model parity is limited by HW and vendor kernels; don't promise identical latency.
- Any route-level fallback should include a mandatory audit trail for compliance-sensitive customers.

Suggested owners and next steps (short)
----
- Obs/Console: implement percentile telemetry and export (owner: Diego Alvarez) — schedule: 2w for initial dash
- Serving/runtime + Routing: prototype fallback policy + audit events (owner: Priya Nair) — spike: 3w
- Private Deployments + Applied ML: define model pack scope and verification checklist (owner: Maya Thompson) — kickoff: next sprint
- DevEx: draft streaming stability kit and SDK snippets (owner: Jordan Lee) — deliverable: PR with examples in 3w

Communications & customer follow-up
----
- Share this doc with pilot customers and invite 30-min feedback session.
- For top-3 customers who raised latency/fallback concerns, propose a "health-check" call with SRE + solutions Eng to review traffic patterns and mitigation plan.

Unresolved questions / input needed
----
- Product: do we want "fallback" to be a Console-configurable policy for hosted customers, or should it remain engineering-driven?
- Legal: any restrictions on distributing quantized model weights to Private customers? (ask legal)
- Applied ML: tolerance threshold guidance for quality loss during fallback — what metric(s) should we surface?

Raw appendix (snippets from tickets)
----
- Ticket #CCS-4021: "Nightly batch jobs run on a quantized variant and outputs sometimes mismatch the hosted model by X% — need deterministic mapping."
- Email excerpt: "If fallback occurs, product managers want both an event and a human-friendly summary of what changed."
- Pilot retrospective note: "Autoscale recovered but customer saw 1m window of degraded quality; they want a replayable trace to show to compliance."

Bottom line
----
Customers are asking for observability and policy primitives that make degradation predictable and explainable. Start with telemetry + simple fallback policy primitives; parallel-track private compatibility work. Prioritize quick, demonstrable wins to reduce escalations while designing the longer policy/runtime features carefully to avoid surprising behavior.
